title: Granny triangle
subtitle: A three-corner granny motif for diagonal layouts and edge filling
excerpt: The granny triangle uses three corner positions instead of four, giving an equilateral triangle that fills the gaps when granny squares are set on-point in a diagonal layout. Three rounds in DK cotton produce a tile that fits exactly into the corner gap between four squares arranged in a diamond.
sourceNotes: Weldon's Practical Crochet, Volume 2 (1887), triangular motif chapter (Internet Archive).
heroPrompt: A granny triangle crochet motif in dusty rose DK cotton on a pale linen background, photographed flat from above in soft daylight. Three cluster-and-chain-2 corners visible, 9 cm across the base.

crochet.gaugeText: Finished granny triangle measures approximately 9 cm along the base in DK-weight cotton with a 4 mm hook.

chartDefinition.title: Granny triangle
chartDefinition.caption: Three corner chain-2 spaces. Cluster pairs between corners on each side. Three rounds from the magic ring.

glossaryTerms.definition: Setting square motifs at a 45-degree angle so the corners point up, down, and sideways. The diamond-shaped gaps created at the edges are filled with granny triangles or granny half-squares.

content.text: The granny triangle works the same cluster-and-corner structure as the granny square but with three corners instead of four. It was designed for
, where granny squares set at 45 degrees leave triangular gaps at the edges that need filling.

Work three rounds from the magic ring. Round 1 sets three corner spaces with one cluster pair per corner. Rounds 2 and 3 add side clusters between corners. The triangle joins along any side at the cluster chain spaces.

attrs.title: Materials for one motif
attrs.body: About 4 g of DK-weight cotton. A 4 mm hook. Tapestry needle and scissors.

content.text: Magic ring. Ch 3 (counts as first tr). 2 tr into ring. *Ch 2, 3 tr into ring.* Rep 2 more times. Ch 2. Sl st to top of beg ch-3. Pull ring closed. (9 tr, 3 ch-2 corner spaces.)
Sl st to first ch-2 corner sp. Ch 3. Into same sp: 2 tr, ch 2, 3 tr. *Ch 1, into next ch-2 corner sp: 3 tr, ch 2, 3 tr.* Rep from * twice more. Ch 1. Sl st to join. (6 clusters, 3 corners.)
Sl st to corner sp. Ch 3. Into same sp: 2 tr, ch 2, 3 tr. *Ch 1, 3 tr into side ch-1 sp. Ch 1, into next corner sp: 3 tr, ch 2, 3 tr.* Rep from * around. Ch 1. Sl st to join. Fasten off.
For a larger triangle, add further rounds with an extra cluster per side each time. Or work the star motif five-point for a more complex multi-section shape.
